title: Finance & Legal: Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition Playbook
author: Ava Thompson
content:
Summary:
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's standard processes and controls for budgeting and forecasting, procurement, contracts/legal review, and revenue recognition & billing. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement, and business owners who execute or approve financial commitments. The goal is consistent, auditable decisions that meet compliance requirements and preserve runway and unit economics.

Scope:
- Applies to all spend and contract commitments across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private product lines.
- Includes capital and operating budgets, vendor procurement, contract lifecycle steps, purchase order (PO) processing, invoicing, revenue recognition, and billing operations.
- Excludes personal expense policy (see company-handbook).

1) Budgeting & Forecasting
Intro and Principles:
- Annual bottom-up budgeting aligned with quarterly rolling forecasts. Budgets are owned by product & functional leads and consolidated by Finance.
- Key principles: accuracy within +/- 5% for top-line commit; transparent assumptions; scenario planning for +/- 10% and +/- 25% demand shocks.

Calendar & Deliverables (example cadence):
1. July: Planning kickoff and assumptions collection for next fiscal year.
2. August-September: Department-level draft budgets (OMG Template v2).
3. October: Finance consolidation and executive review.
4. November: Final budget approved by CFO & CEO; board materials prepared.
5. Ongoing: Rolling forecast updated monthly with variance commentary.

Budgeting Inputs & Models:
- Revenue inputs: ARR cohorts, churn assumptions, new customer ramp, product mix (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).
- Cost inputs: cloud/GPU spend forecast (by region and instance type), headcount by role and ramp schedule, third-party license & vendor costs, and expected capital expenditures (CAPEX) for hardware.
- Sensitivity tests: GPU cost per token +/- 20%, 10% change in average sequence length, 15% change in request volume.

Approval & Change Control:
- Budget sign-off: Department head -> Finance FP&A -> CFO -> CEO for material changes (>5% of department budget).
- Budget reforecasting: material changes (>=10% delta vs prior forecast) must include remediation plan and be reviewed by Finance.

2) Procurement Procedures
Objectives:
- Minimize procurement cycle time while enforcing controls and securing favorable commercial terms.

Procurement Steps (standard):
1. Requirement & budget validation: requestor fills Procurement Request Form (PRF) in internal portal and confirms budget availability code.
2. Preferred vendor check: Procurement team verifies vendor against Preferred Vendor List (PVL).
3. Competitive sourcing: For > $50,000 expected spend, obtain at least 2 bids (unless sole-source justification approved).
4. Commercial terms & negotiation: Procurement coordinates with Legal for non-standard terms.
5. PO issuance: Procurement issues PO; no vendor work without signed PO/contract and PO# unless exception approved.
6. Receipt & invoice matching: Accounts Payable (AP) matches invoice to PO and receipt; 3-way match for goods/services > $5,000.

Approval Matrix (summary - use for PO creation):
- <$5,000: Manager approval (email approval allowed).
- $5,000- $50,000: Director approval + Budget owner.
- $50,000- $250,000: VP approval + Procurement lead + Legal consult if > 1 year term or data access.
- >$250,000: CFO approval + Legal + Procurement + Executive sponsor.

Payment & Vendor Onboarding:
- Payment terms default to Net 30 unless procurement negotiates Net 45 or Net 60 for strategic vendors.
- Vendor onboarding requires W-9/CTC (or equivalent) and security questionnaire for vendors with access to customer data.
- For cloud/GPU providers, attach consumption forecasts and tagging requirements for cost allocation.

Exception Handling:
- Emergency spend (time-sensitive infra repairs) can be approved by SRE lead + Finance on-call and must be documented within 3 business days.

3) Contracts & Legal Process
Contract Lifecycle Overview:
- Request -> Template selection -> Commercial terms negotiation -> Legal review -> Signature -> Execution & storage -> Obligations tracking -> Renewal/termination.

SLAs & Time-to-Review Targets:
- Standard SaaS Master Services Agreement (MSA) or Redwood-approved PSA: Legal turnaround target 3 business days.
- Non-standard terms (privacy, security, IP, indemnity): target 7-10 business days depending on complexity.
- Expedited review: option to request 24-48 hour turnaround in exchange for prioritized resource; must be justified by executive sponsor.

Signature Authority:
- Individual contributors: may negotiate terms only with explicit manager approval; cannot sign.
- Director-level and below: may sign NDAs and low-value contracts <$25,000 when pre-approved template is used.
- VP: may sign contracts up to $250,000 with Legal countersignature.
- CFO/CEO: required signatures for contracts > $250,000 or material legal obligations (data residency, indemnity caps, revenue commitments).

Mandatory Clauses & Standards:
- Use Redwood-approved templates for MSA, SOW, NDA, and Vendor Agreement.
- Data protection addendum required for vendors processing customer or sensitive data.
- Insurance: minimum general liability limits and cyber insurance proof required for vendors with sensitive access.

Contract Storage & Tracking:
- All fully executed contracts must be uploaded to the Contract Repository (link in portal) within 48 hours.
- Owner must create/update Contract Tracker entry: counterparty, effective date, expiration, auto-renewal terms, termination window, financial commitments, and SLA credits.

4) Revenue Recognition & Billing Policies
Principles:
- Redwood recognizes revenue in accordance with ASC 606 (or IFRS 15), recognizing revenue when performance obligations are satisfied.
- For subscription-based Hosted API: recognize ratably over the service period unless usage-based performance obligations require variable consideration handling.

Billing & Invoicing:
- Billing cadence: default monthly invoicing in arrears for consumption-based Hosted API; annual or quarterly invoicing for committed Dedicated capacity as negotiated.
- Invoice contents: invoice date, invoice number, PO number (if applicable), service period, line-item detail (product, units, unit price), taxes, payment instructions.
- Invoice delivery: electronic delivery via billing portal and e-mail to billing contact.
- Standard payment terms: Net 30; exceptions require Finance approval and updated contract language.

Variable Consideration & Credits:
- Usage-based discounts, credits for downtime (SLA credits) or refunds must be computed in accordance with contract terms and documented.
- Credits are applied to the next invoice unless customer requests a refund (refunds require Finance + Sales approval for > $5,000).

Revenue Deferral & Recognition Examples:
- Prepaid annual Dedicated contract: record as deferred revenue at receipt and recognize over the contracted period (monthly amortization).
- Consumption-based invoice billed in arrears: recognize revenue in month usage occurred; accruals are used for month-end close where billing is not yet invoiced.
- Contract modification with material price change: evaluate as separate contract or prospectively adjust revenue recognition per ASC 606 guidance.

Dunning, Collections & Disputes:
- Dunning cadence: reminder at 7 days overdue, escalation at 30 days (Account Manager notif), final notice at 60 days (collections team engaged).
- Dispute SLA: Billing disputes must be acknowledged within 48 business hours and resolved within 10 business days where feasible.
- Write-offs: AP/AR write-offs > $10,000 require CFO approval and documented evidence of collection attempts.

Tax & Compliance:
- Sales tax/VAT is applied per billing address and customer tax status. Finance maintains Nexus & VAT registration map.
- For cross-border contracts, ensure ECCN and export controls review for models and on-prem deployments when required.

5) Reporting, Controls & Auditability
Required Reports & Retention:
- Monthly: revenue by product, deferred revenue schedule, aging AR, large credit memos.
- Quarterly: variance analysis to forecast, significant contract amendments, and revenue recognition memos for material deals.
- Retention: financial records and contracts retained for 7 years (longer where required by law or customer contract).

Segregation of Duties & Controls:
- Procurement requestor cannot approve same PO above manager level.
- Legal reviews all term exceptions that change indemnity, liability, or revenue impact.
- Finance performs monthly reconciliations between Contract Tracker, Billing Ledger, and General Ledger.

Audit & External Requests:
- Finance acts as primary contact for external audits. Provide contract repository exports, billing ledger exports, and GL reconciliations within standard audit timelines (30 days unless extended).
